title: Scheduler Experimentation and Observable Fidelity Manual
author: Asha Patel
content:
# Scheduler Experimentation and Observable Fidelity Manual

Summary
-------
This manual documents the recommended process, observability signals, and bench/experiment templates for running scheduler and kernel-selection experiments on the Redwood serving runtime. It ties runtime architecture considerations to scheduler policy changes, prescribes profiling and benchmarking steps, and provides a safe rollout / rollback runbook for production canaries. The intent is to make scheduler experiments repeatable, measurable, and auditable while protecting customer SLOs.

Goals
-----
- Provide a repeatable experiment skeleton for kernel/scheduler changes.
- Define the fidelity and telemetry signals required to qualify a change for canary and global rollout.
- Define bench and replay artifacts to measure cost/latency impact and guard against degradation.
- Standardize rollout criteria, rollback triggers, and owner responsibilities.

Scope and non-goals
-------------------
- In scope: scheduler policy language changes, kernel hinting heuristics, admission controller tuning, telemetry-driven adaptive policies.
- Out of scope: model architecture changes, client-side retry behaviour, or infra provisioning (handled by eng-infra).

Audience
--------
- Runtime engineers implementing scheduler logic and kernel authors.
- SRE and oncall for canary/production validation.
- Applied ML / perf teams running fidelity and cost experiments.

Principal components referenced (service names)
---------------------------------------------
- runtime-coordinator: global experiment controller and policy reconciler.
- kernel-agent: per-node kernel selection and hinting process.
- telemetry-pipeline: trace/metric collector and enrichment layer (ingest + partitioner).
- perf-lab: synthetic benchmark runner and mirror replay harness.
- autoscaler: capacity and burst handling component.

SLOs & safety thresholds (operational baseline)
---------------------------------------------
- Short-seq p95 latency (<= 64 tokens): target 60 ms, hard SLO 120 ms.
- p99 latency (<= 64 tokens): target 120 ms, alert at 200 ms.
- 95th-percentile GPU kernel-run-time variance increase: <= 10% relative to baseline during canary.
- Error rate increase: <= 0.05% absolute over baseline in canary window.
- Cost-per-token delta: treat increases > 8% as economic regression.

Telemetry and observability: required signals
-------------------------------------------
The following signals must be captured and correlated for every scheduler experiment:
1) Request-level traces (span naming: runtime.request -> scheduler.decision -> kernel.dispatch) with the following attributes: model, route, sequence_length, priority_class, admission_decision, kernel_variant.
2) Kernel-level histograms: dispatch_duration_ms, execution_duration_ms, occupancy_pct, tensor_core_util_pct.
3) Queue and admission metrics: queue_depth_by_route, admission_rejections, preemption_events.
4) Cost signals: tokens_generated, gpu_ms_charged, per-request-cost-estimate.
5) Sampling artifacts: 1% full-request-body capture (shadow only, redaction required), 10% top-k token histogram.

Instrumentation checklist (must exist before experiment start)
---------------------------------------------------------------
- runtime-coordinator event emitted for experiment start/end and policy version.
- kernel-agent emits kernel_variant tag with kernel_hash.
- telemetry-pipeline enrichment populates "kernel_variant" and "scheduler_policy_id" fields and writes to perf-lab topic.
- Perf Lab replay mapping for route -> synthetic corpus present (see Appendix B).

Experiment taxonomy and examples
-------------------------------
A. Kernel hinting heuristic change (low blast radius)
- Change: prefer FP16 kernel variant for sequence_length < 128 when occupancy > 45%.
- Risk: reduced numeric fidelity for edge tokens.
- Typical runtime config change: kernel_hint.profile=fp16_aggressive, kernel_hint.min_occupancy=45

B. Admission controller tightening (medium blast radius)
- Change: limit speculative-batch admission for non-premium routes during peak windows.
- Risk: increased latency for eligible batched requests (due to single-run path).
- Runtime config: admission.speculative_batch.enabled=false for routes [chat-api-v2], window=18:00-22:00 UTC

C. Scheduler policy language rewrite (high blast radius)
- Change: integrate economic-priority in policy DSL and add preemption budgets.
- Risk: complex decision pathways may introduce priority inversions.
- Requires perf-lab shadow replay prior to canary and an extended canary window (72h).

Profiling playbook (step-by-step)
--------------------------------
1) Pre-experiment profiling (dev cluster)
  - Run perf-lab synthetic suite: ./perf-lab run --experiment <id> --profile baseline --topology small-mixed.
  - Collect kernel-level traces: ensure kernel-agent trace rate at 100% for dispatched kernels in this run.
  - Generate comparison report: compare dispatch_duration_ms / execution_duration_ms histograms to baseline.

2) Shadow traffic validation (staging)
  - Mirror 10% of production traffic for 2 hours into staging using traffic-mirroring-service.
  - Validate that telemetry-pipeline enrichments and trace correlation tags are present.
  - Run automated fidelity checks: BLEU/ROUGE spot-checks for sample responses when applicable.

3) Canary (production, isolated cohort)
  - Scope: 1% of traffic or a single small region (preferably non-critical).
  - Duration: 24h minimum, extendable based on risk category (see taxonomy).
  - Metrics to monitor live: short-seq p95/p99, error_rate, admission_rejections, kernel_variant_latency_delta, cost-per-token.
  - Automated rollback triggers (see Runbook section).

4) Extended monitoring and rollout
  - If canary stable for window, expand to 10% for 48h and re-evaluate.
  - Run perf-lab long-run cost simulation for 7 days to capture diurnal effects.

Benchmarking suite integration
-----------------------------
- Bench artifacts to generate for every experiment:
  1) Microbench: per-kernel latency/throughput at multiple sequence lengths and batch sizes.
  2) Shadow replay: 24h replay of sampled production surface with kernel_variant toggles.
  3) Cost-sim: per-route cost impact across synthetic and replay workloads.

Sample benchmarking job JSON (perf-lab)
--------------------------------------
{
  "job": "scheduler-experiment-<id>",
  "targets": ["kernel-variants", "routes"],
  "duration": "24h",
  "replay_topic": "perf-lab.replay.scheduler-experiment-<id>",
  "metrics": ["p95_latency","p99_latency","gpu_ms_charged","kernel_dispatch_variance"]
}

(Place this in perf-lab jobs directory and ensure replay_topic is provisioned in telemetry-pipeline.)

Release notes checklist (for runtime release carrying scheduler changes)
---------------------------------------------------------------------
- Summary line describing high-level risk and affected routes.
- List of config flags and default values.
- Canary plan referencing this manual and experiment id.
- Telemetry migration notes (schema changes, new tags).
- Rollback instructions and quick commands.

Known issues and mitigations (experiment-related)
------------------------------------------------
- Issue: kernel_variant tag not propagated to long-term metrics store.
  - Mitigation: add temporary joiner job in telemetry-pipeline to backfill kernel_variant via trace correlation.
- Issue: admission.rejections spike without latency change (indicates over-aggressive admission policy).
  - Mitigation: revert admission window and enable speculative ramp for target routes.
- Issue: Perf-lab replay underestimates tail-latency due to missing network latencies.
  - Mitigation: add network-latency augmentation step to replay harness (see Appendix A).

Runbook: Canary quick actions (operational)
-----------------------------------------
1) Detect: alert triggers when p99 short-seq latency > 150 ms or error_rate delta > 0.05%.
2) Triage: oncall page -> add incident tag `scheduler-experiment-<id>`; notify runtime-policy-owner and kernel-owner.
3) Quick rollback: run (requires runtime-coordinator access):
   - curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
     https://runtime-coordinator.internal/api/v1/experiments/<id>/rollback
   - Alternatively: set runtime-coordinator policy_deactivate=true for policy id.
4) Postmortem: collect perf-lab job artifacts, full traces (use runbook `operator-livetrace-collection-and-rollback-playbook-2027`), and open postmortem ticket with severity, timeline, and owner.

Owner and escalation matrix
---------------------------
- Experiment owner: runtime-scheduler team (oncall: @runtime-scheduler).
- Kernel variant owner: kernel-team (oncall: @kernel-oncall).
- SRE escalation: runtime-sre (pager rotation).

Configuration table (recommended starting defaults)
--------------------------------------------------
Parameter | Default | Notes
---------|---------|------
kernel_hint.profile | conservative_fp16 | safe default that prefers stability
kernel_hint.min_occupancy | 50 | percent, reduce aggressive switching below this
admission.speculative_batch.enabled | true | set false only in targeted canaries
admission.max_batch_size | 64 | avoid >64 for short-seq heavy routes
scheduler.preemption_budget_ms | 100 | per-GPU per-minute budget for preemption

Appendix A — Network augmentation for perf-lab replay
----------------------------------------------------
- Add a synthetic latency layer to perf-lab Docker network: tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem delay 8ms 4ms distribution normal.
- Documented in perf-lab job by adding "netem_delay_ms": 8.

Appendix B — Replay mapping example
----------------------------------
- Map production route `chat-api-v2` -> replay corpus `chat-api-v2-2026-11-sampled-24h`
- Replay config snippet: 
  replay_map:
    - route: chat-api-v2
      corpus: chat-api-v2-2026-11-sampled-24h
      sample_rate: 0.12

Appendix C — Useful CLI snippets
--------------------------------
- Start a perf-lab job: perf-lab submit --job-file jobs/scheduler-experiment-<id>.json
- Query canary metrics: curl -s "https://metrics.internal/api/query?experiment=<id>&window=1h" | jq .
- Force rollback (runtime-coordinator): kubectl -n runtime exec svc/runtime-coordinator -- \
  -- ./runner rollback --experiment <id> --reason "ops-triggered-rollback"

Document maintenance and ownership
----------------------------------
- This manual is owned by the eng-serving-runtime / runtime-scheduler subteam.
- Update cadence: every major scheduler release or after a canary that resulted in rollback.
- Related pages: add postmortems and perf-lab job ids under related_pages.

If you are about to run an experiment and this manual does not fully answer your questions, open a PR to this doc and tag @Miguel Torres for review.
